open: [STUB] Ring Two's food stalls are noisy again, the market lines folding around one counter where the stallholder holds up a receipt for forty bowls. Across from her, an off-shift crew holds up its own receipt for the same order. She says they never collected. Their boss says they collected and paid twice. If nobody settles it before the market bell, the crew boycotts her stall and the Exchange clerk logs a complaint against whoever let it stand. Minutes remain.

clean.text: [STUB] Onions fry somewhere above while the stallholder counts on her fingers, twenty bowls lost against a crew lost for the season. She tears both receipts down the middle and pins one half of each to her post. Their boss shakes on it across the counter. Word of the even split runs along Ring Two before the bell, and two neighbouring stalls nod your crew through the line.

cost.text: [STUB] Half is not enough for her; she wants a thousand credits from your side before she budges. Coins ring into her cash tin, counted twice under her breath. Across the counter, the boss folds his receipt away. Grease pencil goes through the forty-bowl order on her board, marked settled, and the stall keeps its regulars past the bell.

fail.text: [STUB] Counting her losses only hardens her, because twenty bowls is a full day of beans. No split, she says. Behind them, the crew boss marches his people two stalls down to buy elsewhere. A finger jabs toward the Exchange clerk's desk: bring it there at first shift tomorrow, both receipts in hand. Your crew carries the argument home in tight shoulders.

clean.text: [STUB] Two stalls over, a loader argues with a scanner while the stallholder hovers over her own books. Her receipt printer holds the answer: its counter jumped twice on one payment, printing the crew's copy and hers from a single sale. Nobody owes anybody bowls. Red-faced, she reprints a corrected slip, and their foreman laughs loud enough to loosen every shoulder on your side of the counter.

cost.text: [STUB] Under the scale tray sits a folded shim, and the tare reading doubles every crate set on it. That explains the second charge on the crew's receipt. Grinning, the foreman counts five hundred credits into your crew's hands, his forty bowls still warm in their crates. Behind the counter the stallholder pulls the shim and stares hard at your people. Prices for them go up tonight.

fail.text: [STUB] Books snap shut under her palm before the second page turns. Hovering becomes shouting. Without her ledger the twin receipts prove nothing, and five hundred credits from your crew's purse go into her apron to quiet her before the line sours. The registry office can open a stall's books on request, but it wants fourteen days' notice, long after this bell.

clean.text: [STUB] Down the walk comes the clerk, a stamp swinging on its cord. Her mouth goes thin. One look at both receipts settles it: hers is dated a day late, the crew's is the original. Without a word, she strikes the order off her board. Stamping the ruling, the clerk releases a thousand credits from the Exchange's dispute purse to your crew's tab. Forty bowls go out with their lids on, one stack at a time.

cost.text: [STUB] Clerks do not walk down for free. Before reading either receipt, the clerk writes a 500-credit filing charge against your crew and only then rules: the crew paid twice, and the stallholder refunds it. Glaring past the clerk's shoulder, the stallholder counts out the refund coin by coin. Nobody at this stall will forget who brought the Exchange to her counter.

fail.text: [STUB] Whoever runs for the clerk comes back alone, holding a card from the shut desk: disputes heard at second shift. Calling for an outsider has cost the stallholder's patience. Cloth goes over her pots, and her shoulder turns on everyone at the counter. Your crew wears the glare.

ending: [STUB] Ring Two hums on around the stall, and your crew is still at its counter in Hearthline. A ledger card follows.
